source_quote: The Electrical and Computer Engineering Department (ECE) envisages being a leader
answer: The ECE Department aims to lead in shaping human capital in electrical, computer, communication and biomedical engineering, producing application-oriented graduates, and to be recognized among the best ECE departments in education and research.

source_quote: The ECE Department offers three programs – Electrical Engineering, Computer and
answer: The ECE Department offers three programs - Electrical Engineering, Computer and Communications Engineering, and Biomedical Engineering - each granting BS, BE and MS degrees.

source_quote: The Electrical Engineering program at RHU aims to help students explore their innate
answer: The Electrical Engineering program helps students pursue careers in electrical engineering, solve complex problems with modern tools, communicate and work in diverse teams, and succeed in graduate studies; its objectives include excellence, leadership-oriented professional education, solving societal and industrial problems, and multidisciplinary research.

source_quote: The Electrical Engineering program adopts the learning outcomes of ABET, so our
answer: Electrical Engineering adopts the seven ABET student outcomes: solving complex engineering problems, engineering design, communication, ethical and professional responsibility, teamwork, experimentation and data analysis, and acquiring new knowledge.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Engineering program in Electrical Engineering is accredited by the
answer: The Bachelor of Engineering in Electrical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Electrical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

source_quote: An electrical engineer may work in robotics, computer networks, electric transportation
answer: Electrical engineers can work in robotics, computer networks, electric transportation, medical imaging, renewable energy, the low-power industry and power plants, from large power grids to tiny devices.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Engineering (BE) program in Electrical Engineering comprises 152
answer: The BE in Electrical Engineering is 152 credits over eight regular and three summer semesters; the BS is 118 credits over six regular and three summer semesters. Both require a CGPA, major GPA and Summative Learning Project grade of 70 or above.

source_quote: BS in Electrical Engineering (118 Credits)
answer: BS in Electrical Engineering (118 credits): General Education 27 (23%), College Requirements 24 (20%), Program Requirements 67 (57%); major 49 mandatory, non-major 59 mandatory + 10 elective.

source_quote: BE in Electrical Engineering (152 Credits)
answer: BE in Electrical Engineering (152 credits): General Education 30 (20%), College Requirements 27 (18%), Program Requirements 95 (62%); major 59 mandatory + 15 elective, non-major 65 mandatory + 13 elective.

source_quote: ELEC 533 Advanced Machines and Drives 3 ELEC 331, 432
answer: Electrical Engineering mandatory courses: CCEE 221/221L, 331, 341, 426/426L, 460/460L, 534; ELEC 200, 301/301L, 320/320L, 323, 330, 331/331L, 340, 400 (BS project; BE takes a technical elective instead), 405, 406, 431, 432/432L, 451, 499 Co-op, 533, 534, 563, 595A, 595B; and MECH 333.

answer: BE Electrical students take 15 credits of engineering technical electives and must have senior standing to take them; focus areas are Power, Renewable Energy and Intelligent Systems. Electives from other programs need advisor and instructor approval.

source_quote: ELEC 433 High Voltage Engineering 3 ELEC 330
answer: Electrical technical electives include ELEC 433 High Voltage Engineering, 434 Power Distribution, 444 Electromagnetic Compatibility, 498 Special Topics, 503 Artificial Neural Systems, 504 Lasers, 531 Power Systems for Transportation, 532 Power Electronics in Power Systems, 535 Renewable Energy for the Built Environment, 536 Renewable Energy Systems, 542 Advanced Power Electronics, 551 Nonlinear Adaptive Control, 560 Sustainable Energy, 561 Wind Energy, 562 Solar Energy, and 597 Advanced Topics.

source_quote: Students must complete a 3-credit-hour course for BS (4 credits for BE; taken 1 credit in
answer: The Electrical Engineering SLP is 3 credits for the BS and 4 credits for the BE (1 credit then 3 credits in consecutive regular semesters), done preferably in groups on an industry or community problem.

source_quote: Students must complete 8 weeks of practical training in a field related to their interests.
answer: Electrical engineering students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (ELEC 499), usually in the summer of the third year, with faculty follow-up, a formal report, poster and presentation; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites.

source_quote: 0: General; 1: Electrical; 2: Electronics; 3: Power; 4: Magnetism; 5: Control
answer: ELEC course codes 'ELEC abc': a = year/level; b = focus area (0 General, 1 Electrical, 2 Electronics, 3 Power, 4 Magnetism, 5 Control); c = sequence. Example: ELEC 320 is the first second-year Electronics course.

source_quote: Year 1, Summer Semester (10 Credits)
answer: Electrical Year 1 Summer (10 credits): CCEE 221L, MATH 311, Humanities/Fine Arts Elective I, Science Elective. Year 2 Fall (17 credits): CCEE 331, ELEC 301/301L, ELEC 320/320L, ENGL 217, MATH 351.

source_quote: ELEC 340 Engineering Electromagnetics 3 PHYS 211
answer: Electrical Year 2 Spring (17 credits): ELEC 323, ELEC 330, ELEC 331/331L, ELEC 340, MATH 314, and a Community and Sustainability Elective. Year 2 Summer (9 credits): ENGR 300, MATH 421, Social Science Elective I.

answer: Electrical Year 3 Fall (16 credits): CCEE 426/426L, ELEC 405, ELEC 406, ELEC 431, ELEC 451. Year 3 Spring (17 credits): CCEE 341, CCEE 460/460L, ELEC 432/432L, Technical Elective 1 or BS Project, MECH 333.
